raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

When a target-token scoring request opts into prefix-cache reads, a cache hit can skip rows whose scores are required. This PR bounds reuse at `prompt_logprob_start` so every requested score is returned. Implements the bounded-KV step of #60366 and M1 of #62175.

Related work on prefix-cache reuse for prompt scoring: #60960. This PR resolves unsupported configurations before connector admission, checks the worker-resolved KV format, and adds complete-score regressions.

## Claims

- With `skip_reading_prefix_cache=False`, scoring requests reuse KV before the first scored row and return the complete score matrix.
- Defaults and ordinary generation are unchanged. Unsupported configurations, and requests that also ask for ordinary prompt logprobs, recompute the full prompt and log a one-time warning.
- With Qwen3-32B at TP=4, teacher scoring is 3.7x to 3.8x faster for long shared documents and about 1.1x faster for short prompts.

## Validation

| Setup | Check | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Single GPU | Cache and scheduler suites | 447 passed (2 multi-GPU cases excluded) |
| Qwen3-0.6B, TP=1 | Eager and CUDA-graph scoring with async scheduling; incomplete-buffer rejection | 2 GPU tests and 1 CPU test passed |
| Qwen3-0.6B-FP8, TP=1 | 7 cache-boundary cases with FP8 weights and 16-bit KV | Passed |
| 2×A40 and 4×A40, Qwen3-0.6B | 32-response replay, cache boundaries, forced prefill preemption at TP=2 and TP=4 | Complete outputs, exact match with uncached scoring in batch-invariant mode |

### Teacher-stage performance

Qwen3-32B, 4×A100 80GB with NVLink, TP=4, BF16, FlashAttention 2, compilation and CUDA graphs, synchronous scheduling. Batch-invariant mode is off. Each prompt group has four responses and starts with an empty cache. Each case alternates six repetitions per path after warmup.

The table uses grouped arrivals. Each row covers 16 responses across four groups; times sum the four group medians. The token budget is `max_num_batched_tokens`.

| Token budget | Workload | Uncached | Bounded reuse | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 512 | Short math prompts | 1.88 s | 1.66 s | 1.13x |
| 512 | Long documents | 6.13 s | 1.60 s | 3.84x |
| 2048 | Short math prompts | 1.61 s | 1.42 s | 1.14x |
| 2048 | Long documents | 5.16 s | 1.39 s | 3.71x |

Short prompts have 142 to 209 context tokens and 437 to 1024 response tokens. Documents have 2933 to 3944 context tokens and 13 to 58 response tokens. Staggered arrivals, targeting 20 ms gaps with admission at engine-step boundaries, gave similar results: 1.11x to 1.13x for short prompts and 3.71x to 3.83x for documents. Across all six repetitions, aggregate speedups ranged from 1.11x to 1.14x for short prompts and 3.66x to 3.87x for documents. These are offline scoring times, including the existing one-token generation step; model loading, compilation and warmup are excluded.

BF16 scores vary with execution shape. The largest absolute logprob difference from uncached scoring on the 32B runs was 0.50, compared with 0.37 between single and batched uncached scoring. A separate Qwen3-0.6B synthetic probe reached 0.14 for actual tokens and 1.17 for extra candidates. Batch-invariant Qwen3-0.6B checks matched exactly across uncached, bounded and preempted paths. Training loss and gradient validation is part of the VIME integration.

Scripts, raw results and pinned source/model versions: [reproduction materials in my fork](https://github.com/LinzeShi/vllm/blob/db215c5db9eec0decd891b802b2928f90fe16d46/benchmarks/opd_prefix_reuse_tp4/README.md).

<details>
<summary>Test commands</summary>

The scoring command below uses `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=warn`. A40 GPU checks also passed with `error`.

```bash
# Local single-GPU validation. Omit the filter on a multi-GPU host.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q \
  -k 'not test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders and not test_diffusion_read_deferral_keeps_a_longer_pp_wait'
# Scoring checks.
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=warn \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py -q \
  -k 'bounded_prefix_reuse or reject_incomplete_prefill'
```

</details>

## Details

KV holds attention state, not the logits for skipped rows. The cache hit is capped at `min(prompt_logprob_start or 0, num_tokens - 1)` with the usual block alignment, and the cap applies again after preemption. Admission decides the fallback before connector hooks run, on a copy of the caller's sampling params.

The first version uses MRV2 and supports text token inputs, one causal full-attention KV group, unquantized KV, `max_tokens=1`, and single-GPU or tensor-parallel execution. It adds no response fields and no score storage. Connector, adapter and other configuration exclusions are documented in `docs/training/prompt_token_id_logprobs.md`.

---

<details>
<summary>Pull Request Checklist</summary>

- [x] **Design Fit:** Reuses the cache coordinator and existing scoring worker.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Single-GPU and TP=2/4 replay, complete-score regressions, and teacher-stage measurements.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Existing suites extended, documentation updated, checks passed.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Motivation, related work, evidence and limitations included.

</details>

@@ -55,12 +55,31 @@ lists of Python ints are much slower to copy and serialize. With a logits
 - The longest row at most `--max-logprobs` candidates.
 - No `--kv-sharing-fast-prefill`.
 
-The request skips reading the prefix cache (local and KV connector), since
-cached rows have no logits to score.
+By default, the request skips reading the prefix cache (local and KV connector),
+since cached rows have no logits to score.
+
+## Reusing the context prefix
+
+Set `skip_reading_prefix_cache=False` to reuse local KV before
+`prompt_logprob_start`. Every requested scoring row is still computed, even if
+the cache contains a previous copy of the entire response. Cache hits are rounded
+down to the available block boundary. For example, a 2048-token context has
+`prompt_logprob_start=2047`; with 16-token blocks, at most 2032 tokens are reused.
+
+This path supports text token inputs, one causal full-attention KV group,
+unquantized KV, `max_tokens=1`, and single-GPU or tensor-parallel
+execution. Chunked prefill and prefill preemption retain the scoring boundary.
+The generated token is still returned; scoring callers can discard it.
+
+Requests that also ask for ordinary `prompt_logprobs` use full recomputation.
+So do configurations with KV/offload connectors, auxiliary
+output capture, hybrid or sliding-window attention, partial-block reuse,
+multimodal inputs or prompt embeddings, LoRA, speculative decoding, resumable
+sessions, or other parallel topologies. The existing input validation still
+applies. Neither the scoring output format nor the no-read default changes.
+An unsupported opt-in configuration logs a warning once before falling back.
 
 ## Limitations
 
 - Non-streaming only; `stream=true` requests are rejected.
 - Not exposed through the OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
-- If a prefill starts past the first scored row (e.g. `skip_reading_prefix_cache=False`
-  with a cache hit), the result is `None` rather than a partial matrix.
